method: Targeted manual inspection of four existing candidates and supplied evidence. No new model calls. Cases are illustrative, not randomly sampled or a representative human evaluation.
conclusion: Real missing-context and attribution defects remain; subjective usefulness filtering and inconsistent verifier explanations also remain. These four cases cannot quantify how much of the practitioner-versus-lookup acceptance gap is bias. Native audit blocking is not synonymous with an unsupported answer. Frozen common evaluation is still needed.

cases.question: What did Saint Lucia say would determine whether Security Council reform moved forward during the fifty-eighth session?
cases.answer: I expect that the pronouncements made on this issue in the general debate of the fifty-eighth session will determine whether the political will exists to move reform forward.
native_problems: support: The statement is the General Assembly President's expectation, not the position of the State of Saint Lucia. The attribution is wrong.

native_score_notes.anchoring_and_time: 'Security Council reform' and the fifty-eighth session fix the issue and the period well.
native_score_notes.consequence: The span names a concrete criterion: the pronouncements in the general debate will show whether political will exists. It is a statement of expectation, not a decision.
native_score_notes.informativeness: The span fully answers what would determine movement on reform, including the modality 'I expect'.
native_score_notes.linguistic_quality: The question is clear. Attributing it to 'Saint Lucia' is misleading, and the phrase 'said would determine' is slightly loose.
native_score_notes.practitioner_realism: It asks a plausible, bounded question about what would signal political will on Security Council reform.

cases.native_faithfulness_reason: The target supports the answer: the President expects the general-debate pronouncements to determine whether the political will exists to advance reform. The question wrongly credits 'Saint Lucia' and says it 'said' this, but it is the President's expectation. The answer keeps the 'I expect' modality. The fifty-eighth session is correct.
cases.target_block_text:
[EN] Document: A/58/PV.1
  Title: (Saint Lucia)
The General Assembly will have the opportunity to review these important matters when the report of the Security Council comes before it.
As required, I will summarize discussion of the report to inform the future deliberations of the Security Council.
I expect that both the report and the summary will reflect the crises and challenges the United Nations faces in the areas of peace and security.
On the issue of Security Council reform, we cannot retreat from taking a decision on this matter.
For more than a decade, we have deliberated on this issue and have made very little progress.
I expect that the pronouncements made on this issue in the general debate of the fifty-eighth session will determine whether the political will exists to move reform forward.
International standard-setting is an area in which the United Nations has excelled.
Today, multilateral treaties set standards for the promotion and protection of human rights, including the rights of women and children, and govern important areas of international relations, such as transnational crime, the seas, disarmament and the rising challenge of terrorism.
source_excerpts: Opening of the session by the President of the General Assembly
The President: I declare open the fifty-eighth regular session of the General Assembly.
As President of the General Assembly at its fifty-eighth session
cases.assessment: The question attributes a General Assembly presidential expectation to Saint Lucia as a State. Metadata names Saint Lucia, but the supplied context identifies the speaker's presidential role. Native support failure is justified.
cases.caveat: All three candidates are blocking. This case contributes to the target-level acceptance gap.

cases.question: What plan was the Government developing for children who had been separated from their parents in the final stages of the conflict?
cases.answer: In particular, the Government was developing a plan to undertake tracing activities in hospitals, children's homes and police posts through the country;
native_problems: mode: no country, situation or time is given, so the question cannot be resolved to Sri Lanka or to the 2011–2012 period.
anchoring_and_time: the question is generic and lacks a relevant absolute time.

native_score_notes.anchoring_and_time: There is no country (Sri Lanka) and no date or period. "Final stages of the conflict" does not identify any conflict. The question is too generic to retrieve this passage.
native_score_notes.consequence: The tracing plan in hospitals, children's homes and police posts is a concrete measure.
native_score_notes.informativeness: The answer span gives the plan's content directly. The "In particular" lead-in and trailing semicolon are slight extras, and the answer is framed as the Government's development of a plan rather than implementation.
native_score_notes.linguistic_quality: The sentence is clear and grammatical. It slightly misframes the plan as one for separated children when the plan covers tracing.
native_score_notes.practitioner_realism: The need (what plan for tracing separated children) is a plausible bounded one. It lacks the country context, so a specialist could not place it.

cases.native_faithfulness_reason: The target says the Government was developing a plan for tracing activities in hospitals, children's homes and police posts, in the context of tracing children separated from their parents. The question's premise matches. The plan is presented as part of the Special Representative's recalled conclusions, and the question does not attribute it. That is a minor limitation because it is the Government's own act. The answer includes the lead-in 'In particular' and a trailing semicolon, which could be trimmed. It is otherwise complete.

cases.assessment: The question does not identify Sri Lanka, the conflict or a relevant period. Its Government/conflict references are unresolved without the source. The answer is grounded, but native mode failure is justified.
cases.caveat: No candidate at this target has a clear/minor audit. The additional criticism of calling this a plan for separated children is not persuasive; the missing context is sufficient.

cases.question: When States cannot register refugees on their territory, what assistance is requested from the Office of the High Commissioner?
cases.answer: calls upon the Office, as appropriate, to help States to conduct this procedure should they be unable to register refugees on their territory;
native_problems: mode/anchoring_and_time: no time, regime or source context, so the question is underdetermined.

metadata: the anchor 'States cannot register refugees on their territory' is not a verbatim substring; the question says 'When States cannot register refugees on their territory'. The source wording is 'unable to register', but the anchor matches the question text, so it is acceptable.

native_score_notes.anchoring_and_time: The anchor is a generic scenario with no regime, region, period or source attribution. The question could refer to many documents, and there is no time. This is a major weakness.
native_score_notes.consequence: It asks for a concrete requested task, namely the Office helping States conduct registration.
native_score_notes.informativeness: The span gives the requested assistance precisely, with the qualifier 'as appropriate' and the condition. It fully determines the point.
native_score_notes.practitioner_realism: Natural, bounded operational question: what help is UNHCR asked to give when a State cannot register refugees.

cases.native_faithfulness_reason: Paragraph 12 calls upon the Office, as appropriate, to help States conduct registration if they are unable to register refugees on their territory. The answer matches this and preserves 'as appropriate'. 'This procedure' refers to registration, which the question makes clear. No numbers are involved.
source_excerpts: 68/143. Assistance to refugees, returnees and displaced persons in Africa
calls upon the Office, as appropriate, to help States to conduct this procedure should they be unable to register refugees on their territory;
cases.assessment: The question omits relevant time and Africa-specific context, so blocking is defensible under the retained contract. The verifier overstates the lack of any regime context and falsely says an anchor is not a substring before correcting itself. The incorrect metadata explanation is not the reason for the final blocking status.
cases.caveat: Faithfulness is 15/15. All three candidates are blocking. This is not a clean false-positive because retrieval-context defects remain.

cases.question: Who spoke as guests at the 15 April public meeting on business's role in conflict prevention, peacekeeping and post-conflict peace-building?
cases.answer: Guests speakers in the public meeting were the Secretary-General Kofi Annan, the World Bank President, the President and CEO of Siemens, Heinrich von Pierer, the President of the Economic and Social Council, Ambassador Marjatta Rasi, and the Chairman of the Advisory Groups of the Economic and Social Council for African countries emerging from conflict, Ambassador Dumisani Shadrak Kumalo.
native_problems: mode: the question asks for a roster of speakers, which is not a substantive specialist need.
consequence: the answer has low substantive value.

native_score_notes.anchoring_and_time: The date 15 April and the topic identify the meeting well. The year is not in the question but can be inferred from context.
native_score_notes.consequence: A participant list has little normative or operational content. It is roughly ceremonial or procedural.
native_score_notes.informativeness: The answer lists the guest speakers completely, although it keeps the source's typo "Guests speakers".
native_score_notes.linguistic_quality: The question is clear and grammatical. "Business's role" is slightly awkward.
native_score_notes.practitioner_realism: This is a list-of-participants question with little specialist need. It is a low-value factual lookup.

cases.native_faithfulness_reason: Paragraph 39 lists the guest speakers at the 15 April public meeting. The answer reproduces the list, including the source's 'Guests speakers' typo. The date and the topic match the target. The list is the full answer, so nothing is extraneous.
cases.target_block_text:
[EN] Document: S/2004/505
  Title: Letter dated 18 June 2004 from the Permanent Representative of Germany to the United Nations addressed to the Secretary-General I have the honour to enclose the assessment of the work of the Security Council during the presidency of Germany in April 2004 (see annex).
There was agreement that the resolution does not alter existing treaties or arrangements on disarmament, arms control, non-proliferation and verification, which retain their full importance and must be further developed, and that it does not constitute a basis for unilateral enforcement action.
38. Under the terms of the resolution, all Member States are to submit, within the next six months, a first report on steps they have taken or intend to take to implement it.
39. On 15 April, the Council met to discuss the role of business in conflict prevention, peacekeeping and post-conflict peace-building.
Guests speakers in the public meeting were the Secretary-General Kofi Annan, the World Bank President, the President and CEO of Siemens, Heinrich von Pierer, the President of the Economic and Social Council, Ambassador Marjatta Rasi, and the Chairman of the Advisory Groups of the Economic and Social Council for African countries emerging from conflict, Ambassador Dumisani Shadrak Kumalo.
source_excerpts: On 15 April, the Council met to discuss the role of business in conflict prevention, peacekeeping and post-conflict peace-building.
cases.assessment: The target directly supports this specific actor/event question. Categorically rejecting a speaker roster as not a substantive specialist need imports a usefulness preference despite the revised rubric admitting specific events and reported facts. A lower consequence/information-value score is more defensible than automatic mode rejection.
cases.caveat: This is rank3; its rank1 and rank2 siblings are clear. It does not explain the target-level coverage gap. The question also omits the year, so it is not a flawless false-positive. The verifier accepted time by contextual inference here while rejecting omitted time elsewhere.
